title: Amos White's Creole Jazz Band, then Alexandria
summary: After his band broke up he joined Blind Freddie and Amos White; light-skinned players, T-Boy on bass; then Amos left north and Vincent went to Alexandria.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: After my band broke up, you know, the blind Freddie got me with him, you know, with Amos Riley. Then I had Amos Riley with us on the car in the Arlene Creole Jazz Band. Had him with us in there.

And they had all those fellas, looked like white brothers in the band, except me and the bass player, Edda. And the TV car said, what kind of band is this? A higher band? We could play it through. Who was in that band? He said, who was the fellas in that band? Who was the fellas? Them was white. Look out there, man. And Ray T. Gar, he's there too, you know, drummer. He looked like a white fella too. And we had a little girl, Kyle Cook. You know Bill, right? Yeah, yeah. We had him, myself, and Eddie. He didn't have no piano players, you know. And the TV had on cymbal. Betty Babu, yeah. And Betty Babu on cymbal.
Which Eddie was that on bass?
He said, which Eddie was that on bass? What is that? Which Eddie was that you had on bass? Yeah. He was a T-boy. Eddie Gilmore. Yeah. He was called T-boy. Yeah.
Well, who did he play with after he played with Amos White?

So who did you play with after you played with Amos White? Amos White? Amos White. Uh-huh. Yeah. Amos left his and went up the north. And we, we hold up our bag until things got dead. Then we start to go from one place to another, you know. Then I last went to Alexander, you know. Stayed over there about almost four years, you know. Meet a bunch of fellas from here sometime, be over there with us. Like Dr. Noah. Then when I come back, I said, that's back where I tell you. See, I tell you, he picked me up. And then my wife's cousin, he picked me up. And he spoke, hey, you got him, huh? Yeah, yeah.
